# === The Flock - Python Edition ===
# Inspired by Gabriel Lebec's "A Flock of Functions" (2016)

# Primitive birds
I = lambda a: a                                      # Idiot / id
K = lambda a: lambda b: a                            # Kestrel / const
S = lambda f: lambda g: lambda x: f(x)(g(x))        # Starling

# Derived birds (all from SKI)
B = lambda f: lambda g: lambda x: f(g(x))           # Bluebird / compose
C = lambda f: lambda a: lambda b: f(b)(a)           # Cardinal / flip
W = lambda f: lambda x: f(x)(x)                     # Warbler / duplicate
M = lambda a: a(a)                                   # Mockingbird / self-apply
T = lambda a: lambda f: f(a)                         # Thrush / apply / pipe-right
V = lambda a: lambda b: lambda f: f(a)(b)            # Vireo / pair constructor

KI = K(I)   # False / second-selector

# Pair operations via Vireo
pair = V
fst  = lambda p: p(K)
snd  = lambda p: p(KI)

p = pair(1)(2)
print(fst(p), snd(p))   # 1 2

# Church numerals from K and I
zero  = K(I)                             # λf.λx.x -- apply f zero times
once  = lambda f: lambda x: f(x)         # λf.λx.fx -- apply f once
twice = lambda f: lambda x: f(f(x))      # λf.λx.f(fx)

to_int = lambda n: n(lambda k: k + 1)(0)
succ = lambda n: lambda f: lambda x: f(n(f)(x))

print(to_int(zero))   # 0
print(to_int(once))   # 1
print(to_int(twice))  # 2
print(to_int(succ(twice)))  # 3
description: Assemble the primitive and derived combinator birds in Python to build Church pairs and Church numerals.

steps.description: Define the primitive birds I, K, and S alongside the derived birds B, C, W, M, T (Thrush), V (Vireo), and KI = K(I).

steps.answer: V(1)(2) returns lambda f: f(1)(2); passing K selects the first argument 1, and passing KI selects the second argument 2.
steps.question: When p = pair(1)(2) is created with V, how do fst(p) and snd(p) extract 1 and 2?

steps.description: Use Vireo V as pair, K for fst, and KI for snd, then print fst(p) and snd(p) for p = pair(1)(2).
Define Church numerals zero = K(I), once, twice, and succ, and convert each to a Python int using to_int.
Step through fst(p) and snd(p) on line 25 to see the Vireo pair apply K and KI to 1 and 2.

title: The Combinator Flock in Python
